bug_semantics: picklescan classifies pickle GLOBAL/STACK_GLOBAL opcodes as Dangerous only when the (module, name) pair hits its denylist (_suspicious_globals, later renamed _unsafe_globals). logging.FileHandler was never on that denylist through v1.0.0, so a REDUCE payload that instantiates logging.FileHandler(path) scans without a Dangerous finding. Loading the pickle constructs FileHandler in default append mode: a missing path becomes a new zero-byte file at an attacker-chosen location (lock-file / filesystem-pollution DoS); an existing path is opened without overwrite. The scanner itself uses pickletools.genops rather than pickle.loads; the bypass is that downstream users who trust a clean/non-Dangerous scan then deserialize the file.
flaw_origin: The incomplete denylist GLOBAL scanner was first written in c1d5abdcc740e0d08a0d12d015d08e1e6f29a67e (2022-09-04, 'Implement Pickle scanner'). That commit added src/picklescan/scanner.py with _suspicious_globals (eval/compile/getattr/apply, webbrowser/httplib/requests/aiohttp, nt/posix) and scan_pickle_bytes matching that only increments issues when the imported name is listed (lines 14-23 and 84-88). logging.FileHandler is absent from that dict. Parent 6a76b8c3ac67dc04181e600614ecf2a423cca326 is boilerplate only (no src/picklescan/). Later rename to _unsafe_globals (f98f9bd) and expansions such as builtins.open (1c86244) and _io.FileIO (a01c58d) are refactors/additions of the same denylist, not a new first-write of the FileHandler gap. The gap closed only when 4d9bc9cd34bca8672dad3481cd4556d5ba747156 added 'logging': {'FileHandler'}.
